title: Comparative profiling of sperm small RNAs in cnidarians highlights potential for paternal inheritance
abstract: Small RNAs in mature sperm are crucial regulators of gene expression following fertilization during early development in bilaterians. However, the presence and functions of sperm-derived small RNAs remain poorly understood in early-diverging (i.e., non-bilaterian) metazoans. In this study, we characterize three classes of small RNAs—microRNAs (miRNAs), piwi-interacting RNAs (piRNAs), and tRNA-derived RNAs (tDRs)—in sperm from three phylogenetically and ecologically distinct species from the early-diverging phylum Cnidaria: the sea anemone Nematostella vectensis , the temperate stony coral Astrangia poculata , and the reef-building tropical coral Acropora hyacinthus . All three classes of small RNAs examined were present in sperm from these cnidarians. Most miRNAs were species-specific; however, target prediction analysis revealed enriched putative targets involved in conserved developmental and signaling pathways. piRNAs overlapped with transposable elements and genic regions, indicating a potential dual role in genomic maintenance and gene expression regulation. Characterization of tDRs demonstrated that 5’-terminal fragments constituted the primary structural type across the three species, driven by high accumulation of specific isoacceptors including 5’-tDR-GlyGCC. Together, these findings provide the first evidence that cnidarian sperm carry a rich repertoire of small RNAs, including both conserved and species-specific types. Their presence suggests that paternal small RNAs contribute important regulatory information to the zygote in cnidarians, implicating paternal small RNAs as possible mediators of epigenetic inheritance in this early-branching metazoan phylum.

title: Efficacy of chitosan-supported biofilm vaccine against Vibrio parahaemolyticus in Penaeus vannamei.
abstract: Pacific white-leg shrimp, Penaeus vannamei, were immunized by immersion with formalin-inactivated biofilm (BF) and free-cell (FC) preparations of Vibrio parahaemolyticus at 106 CFU/mL for 30 days and evaluated for immune responses, biochemical changes, and disease resistance. Biofilm production was optimized using chitosan particles (10 mg/mL) in tryptone soy broth supplemented with 2% NaCl for 72 h, as confirmed by crystal violet staining, viable bacterial enumeration, and FE-SEM. The optimized biofilm was subsequently used to formulate the inactivated BF vaccine. Following challenge with V. parahaemolyticus (106 CFU/mL), the BF vaccine provided significantly higher protection, with an RPS of 57.15%, compared with FC vaccine group (42.87%). The BF group also exhibited significantly higher total haemocyte count at 72 h post-infection (hpi). Vaccination modulated key innate immune and antioxidant responses, including respiratory burst activity, superoxide dismutase, prophenoloxidase, and catalase activities. In addition, vaccinated shrimp showed improved biochemical profiles, with lower SGOT and SGPT activities and higher total protein, albumin, and globulin levels compared with controls. Overall, the chitosan-supported biofilm vaccine enhanced immunogenicity, improved physiological condition, and conferred greater protection against V. parahaemolyticus infection than the free-cell vaccine. These findings highlight its potential as an immersion-based vaccination strategy for sustainable disease management in P. vannamei aquaculture.

title: Genomic Characterization and Multiplex PCR Authentication of Commercial Triploid Oysters: Evidence for Mosaic Crassostrea gigas-C. angulata Ancestry.
abstract: Triploid oysters are widely used in aquaculture, but their commercial species designation may not accurately represent their nuclear genomic composition, particularly when interspecific or polyploid broodstocks are involved. In this study, we combined whole-genome sequencing with a mitochondrial COI-based multiplex PCR assay to characterize commercial triploid Crassostrea gigas, C. angulata, and C. hongkongensis. Whole-genome allele-frequency analysis confirmed triploidy in all 15 individuals examined, comprising five individuals each from the A3N, G3N, and H3N groups. Cross-species ancestry dosage showed that G3N and H3N were predominantly assigned to their nominal species, whereas A3N exhibited mixed C. angulata-C. gigas nuclear ancestry, with approximately 2.2 and 0.7 haploid-equivalent copies assigned to these species, respectively. The minor C. hongkongensis assignment was interpreted as background cross-assignment rather than evidence of an additional ancestral contribution. Local-ancestry analysis further revealed chromosome-scale mosaics of zero, one, and two C. gigas-derived copies, with copy-weighted C. gigas contributions of approximately 0.69-0.88 haploid-equivalent copies among A3N individuals. This interspecific ancestry was supported by convergent evidence from complementary analyses of discrete dosage-state distributions, D-statistics with two alternative outgroups, and mapping-independent C. gigas-diagnostic 21-mers. All A3N individuals nevertheless carried C. angulata COI haplotypes, consistent with a C. angulata maternal lineage. The breeding history underlying the nuclear ancestry mosaics could not be resolved because the actual parental broodstock was unavailable for genomic analysis. A three-species multiplex PCR assay generated diagnostic products of 212, 359, and 169 bp for C. gigas, C. angulata, and C. hongkongensis, respectively, with no detectable cross-amplification at an optimized annealing temperature of 62 °C. Diagnostic amplification remained detectable with 1 ng of template DNA and was successfully applied to specimens from multiple Korean production sites and Dalian, China. These findings demonstrate complex nuclear ancestry in the five A3N individuals examined that was not captured by their nominal species designation or mitochondrial lineage alone. Although the observed ancestry proportions cannot be generalized to commercial A3N stocks as a whole, the results highlight the complementary roles of genome-wide ancestry analysis and rapid mitochondrial lineage authentication.

title: Testing the mtDNA-Protein Attachment Hypothesis for Doubly Uniparental Inheritance (DUI) of mtDNA in Marine Mussels
abstract: Background: Marine mussels (Mytilus spp.) exhibit a mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) inheritance system known as doubly uniparental inheritance (DUI), in which maternally and paternally transmitted genomes coexist and are independently inherited. One model proposes that M-type mtDNA forms a complex with a nuclear-encoded masculinising protein, based on an electrophoretic mobility shift observed with an M-type control-region probe and male gonadal extracts. A prediction is that this protein should be preferentially enriched with the M-type probe in male gonads and fertilised eggs from male-biased females, compared with corresponding female and F-type probe controls. Methods: We tested this prediction in Mytilus galloprovincialis using electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSA) with biotin-labelled M- and F-type probes, and quantitative shotgun proteomics of pull-down fractions using TMT10plex labelling and LC-MS/MS. Results: EMSA did not detect the expected mtDNA-protein complex, and proteomics identified no statistically significant protein enrichment consistent with model predictions in either gonads or eggs. Conclusions: Although these results do not support the attachment hypothesis under the conditions tested, they provide empirical constraints on a key mechanistic model and highlight the need for complementary approaches, including perinuclear protein enrichment strategies, to resolve the molecular basis of sex determination and paternal mtDNA transmission in bivalves with DUI.

title: Mud Crab Genus Scylla Broodstock Culture: Current Challenges and the Potential of a Hybrid Specific Pathogen Free Approach.
abstract: Mud crab (genus Scylla) farming forms an integral part of coastal aquaculture in Asia region, with their cultivation supporting coastal livelihoods, driving economic growth through their high market demand and promoting mangrove forest conservation and environmental sustainability via mangrove ecosystem integration. However, instability in the production chain, especially the early stages from broodstock cultivation to larval rearing and crablet, promoted the continued reliance on wild-caught broodstock. Such reliance on wild-caught broodstock introduces significant biosecurity risks, particularly through pathogen transmission and inconsistent reproductive performance. Current management selects mature females based on size and ovarian development, followed by acclimation and prophylactic formalin baths to mitigate bacterial and fungal infections. This review examines the biosecurity risks of relying on wild broodstock and proposes a practical "hybrid" approach that combines the innate immune resilience of wild populations with Specific Pathogen Free (SPF)-like conditions to enhance disease resistance, reproductive success and overall production sustainability. Nutritional strategies employ high-protein feeds, such as fish and bivalves, to enhance ovarian maturation, but untreated wild-caught feeds heighten pathogen transmission risks. By quarantine, disinfection and microbiome management protocol, pathogen load can be reduced while innate immunity can be improved. Kaedah penternakan secara ekstensif amat penting dalam akuakultur tropika, kerana ia menyokong mata pencarian penduduk pesisir, memacu pertumbuhan ekonomi melalui permintaan pasaran, dan menggalakkan pemuliharaan hutan bakau serta kelestarian alam sekitar melalui integrasi ekosistem bakau. Namun, ketidakstabilan dalam rantaian pengeluaran, terutamanya pada peringkat awal seperti pemeliharaan induk, penetasan larva dan pembesaran anak ketam telah mengurangkan kecekapan dalam penghasilan ketam dewasa bersaiz pasaran. Kebergantungan terhadap induk tangkapan liar membawa risiko biosekuriti yang ketara, terutamanya melalui transmisi patogen dan prestasi reproduktif yang tidak konsisten. Pengurusan semasa memilih induk betina matang berdasarkan saiz dan kematangan ovari, diikuti dengan proses aklimatisasi dan rendaman formalin secara profilaktik untuk mengurangkan jangkitan bakteria dan kulat. Strategi pemakanan menggunakan makanan berprotein tinggi seperti ikan dan moluska bercangkerang bagi merangsang pematangan ovari, namun penggunaan makanan tangkapan liar yang tidak dirawat meningkatkan risiko transmisi patogen. Melalui protokol kuarantin, pembasmian kuman, pengurusan mikrobiom dan beban patogen dapat dikurangkan, manakala imuniti semula jadi dapat dipertingkatkan.

title: Contrasting Patterns of Seascape Genetics in Acropora cf. tenuis and Their Symbiotic Algae.
abstract: Theory suggests that pairs of mutualist species will often co-disperse and share the same dispersal patterns, though the extent to which this happens remains unclear. Photosynthetic corals constitute an example of this dynamic, as they rely on algal symbionts to meet their energetic needs, yet many acquire their symbionts environmentally after their larval dispersal phase. Consequently, corals and their symbionts may exhibit similar or contrasting patterns of genetic variation across the seascape, with implications for their evolutionary and ecological processes. Here, we densely sample corals of the key reef-building taxon Acropora cf. tenuis and their algal symbionts across a reefscape in the central Philippines to examine genetic variation across space. Four distinct coral taxa show genetic evidence of long-distance dispersal, including weak or absent isolation by distance signals and parent-offspring pairs at widely spaced sites. These coral taxa all host a single group of algal symbionts from the genus Cladocopium, which shows landscape genetic structure independent from its coral hosts. In fact, Cladocopium genetics vary with both latitude and depth, potentially indicating genome-wide local adaptation at a finer spatial scale than that seen in their hosts. Genetic variation at markedly different spatial scales between host and symbiont may be beneficial for hosts if these differences enable them to acquire symbionts adapted to their settlement environments.

title: Genetic architecture of the egg size-number trade-off in the Pacific oyster, Crassostrea gigas.
abstract: The trade-off between egg size and number is a fundamental concept in life-history theory, yet its genetic underpinnings remain poorly characterized in marine invertebrates. In this study, we investigated the genetic architecture of reproductive traits in the Pacific oyster (Crassostrea gigas) using quantitative genetics and genome-wide association analyses. Reproductive traits were measured in 650 offspring, and 220 ripe females were randomly selected for genotyping followed by genome-wide association analysis. We found negative phenotypic and genetic correlations between egg size and egg number. Notably, two variants in the 5' UTR of the TRIM71 locus exhibited opposite allelic effects on the two traits, suggesting a candidate regulatory locus contributing to variation in reproductive allocation. By integrating GWAS with stage-specific transcriptomic profiles, we prioritized candidate genes associated with each trait and identified distinct temporal expression patterns: genes linked to egg size were more highly expressed during early developmental stages, whereas those associated with egg number showed elevated expression during gametogenesis and gonadal ripening. These findings reveal that the egg size-number trade-off in C. gigas is associated with both allelic variation at specific loci and temporally separated expression programs during reproductive development, providing novel insights into the molecular basis of reproductive allocation in marine invertebrates.

title: Genetic Background and Metabolic Influence on Long-Term Lithium Bioaccumulation in Mytilus Mussels and Their Hybrids.
abstract: Marine mussels are widely used as sentinel organisms in coastal biomonitoring, yet the biological mechanisms controlling the bioaccumulation of emerging metals remain poorly constrained. Climate change and anthropogenic disturbances are reshaping species distributions and contact zones, promoting mussel hybridization that may alter physiological traits and contaminant-handling capacities. Lithium (Li) remains largely overlooked despite its potential toxicity and rapidly increasing global demand. Here, we investigate the influence of critical factors on Li bioaccumulation by mussels combining genetic background and isotopic approaches. Progenies of two Mytilus species and their hybrids were transplanted to the same Atlantic coastal site for 12 months. Over this in situ exposure period, Li concentrations show comparable temporal trends across all progeny groups, with an initial uptake-dominated phase followed by biodilution. Lithium isotope ratios (δ7Li) display a coherent temporal trend across all groups (decrease at early exposure, increase during later growth), and the magnitude of the shift differs slightly among genetic backgrounds. Across samples, δ7Li is coupled to growth-related metrics (dry weight) and inversely related to Li concentrations, indicating a metabolic control on Li isotope compositions of these organisms. Li concentrations are also positively correlated with lithogenic-associated elements (e.g., aluminum), consistent with the influence of particle associated Li. A simplified biodynamic modeling including Li isotopes data further indicates a more efficient Li depuration after 5 months, combined with a relatively stronger contribution from dissolved Li. Overall, growth-related factors emerged as the primary biological drivers of Li concentration and isotope variability, with the relative contributions of dissolved and particulate exposure pathways varying in association with physiological growth. Hybridization may modulate Li bioaccumulation and δ7Li values, but its influence appears secondary and does not compromise the use of Mytilus mussels as bioindicators in established frameworks such as "Mussel Watch".

title: Early and Heterogeneous Coral Bleaching Across the Eastern Tropical Pacific During the Fourth Global Coral Bleaching Event
abstract: Abstract Mass coral bleaching is commonly associated with basin-scale heat stress, but its impacts often emerge as spatially uneven mosaics shaped by local oceanography, thermal history, and coral assemblage composition. Here, we compiled 334 opportunistic field observations of coral conditions from 97 sites in six countries of the Eastern Tropical Pacific (ETP), collected between January 2023 and October 2024 through a coordinated regional reporting effort, to document the spatial and temporal expression and taxonomic composition of bleaching during the Fourth Global Coral Bleaching Event. These records provide a regional chronology of observed bleaching, color alteration, and mortality, revealing differences across areas in the timing, duration, and reported condition of bleaching observations. Bleaching observations in the region were concentrated in the second half of 2023, with reports of severe bleaching and mortality mainly in México, El Salvador, Panamá, and Colombia. In Ecuador (Galápagos), bleaching observations extended through 2024 and were dominated by color alteration and partial bleaching rather than widespread mortality. Records were concentrated in the dominant reef-building genera Pocillopora , Porites , and Pavona , although the number and composition of records differed among countries. These observations describe a prolonged and spatially heterogeneous biological response to regional heat stress across the ETP from 2023 to 2024. Our results also emphasize the value of coordinated regional reports for detecting bleaching onset, documenting temporal patterns, and identifying taxa and areas.

title: Temporal Transcriptomic Responses of Turbinaria peltata to Repeated Marine Heatwaves and Recovery Cycles.
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are escalating threats to coral reef ecosystems, yet the host transcriptomic mechanisms underlying acclimatization to repeated thermal stress remain poorly understood. Using de novo RNA sequencing, we tracked the temporal transcriptomic responses of the scleractinian coral Turbinaria peltata across two consecutive MHW-recovery cycles. The second heatwave elicited fewer differentially expressed genes (DEGs) than the first (279 vs. 379), whereas the second recovery phase showed the largest DEG set (399). Functionally, the first heatwave triggered acute stress defense and signal suppression, while the first recovery engaged extracellular matrix remodeling and calcium-mediated tissue repair, indicating incomplete restoration. The largest DEG set during the second recovery indicates that recurrent thermal stress imposes cumulative physiological costs demanding more extensive molecular reorganization-spanning metabolic reprogramming, mTOR and Wnt signaling, and sustained oxidative-stress management. Together with prior physiological and microbiome evidence in this species, our results support a model in which repeated heat exposure progressively shifts the coral host from acute shock defense responses toward compensatory metabolism and structural repair. Recovery thus emerges as an active but increasingly costly molecular adjustment under recurrent MHW regimes. These findings identify candidate molecular markers for evaluating coral resilience under intensifying MHW regimes.

title: Local W-like Haplotype Architecture in the Candidate Sex-Determining Region of Black Tiger Shrimp.
abstract: While female heterogamety in black tiger shrimp (Penaeus monodon) is consistent with a ZW/ZZ system, the sequence organization of its sex-associated region remains unclear. In this study, we examined the candidate sex-determining region on chromosome 19 (2.71-2.89 Mb) using PacBio HiFi reads from a marker-supported ZW female, genotypes from 200 full-sib offspring, local assembly, and public long reads. Three phase blocks overlapped this interval. Sex-associated SNPs assigned W-like and Z-like alleles in two blocks, while the central block remained unoriented. The first block contained gene24, a partial dmd-3-related gene model, and a 54 bp insertion in gene25 intron 1 (INS00000105; INS54). This insertion, supported by 17 W-like HiFi reads and two local assemblers, was called in 100/100 female offspring and 1/99 called males; one male was uncalled. Sanger reads confirmed the insertion and both flanks in three selected market-sourced females and the no-insertion junction in three selected males. Public reads from a Thai female reproduced the insertion-bearing structure, whereas Australian male reads supported the alternative structure. Separate Thai and Chinese long reads crossed the two phase gaps in their respective samples. Together, these results define local female-associated sequence differences and targets for functional investigation, rather than complete W and Z chromosome sequences.

title: Broadcast spawning into a genotoxic environment: Implications on sea urchin (Paracentrotus lividus) embryos.
abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is an oxidative and genotoxic chemical that has widespread use as marine antifoulant treatment, anti-parasitic treatment in finfish farming, and chemical waste discharged from municipal sources. Marine species can experience short-term exposure to high concentrations before dilution and degradation of H2O2. Benthic adult sea urchins spawn gametes directly into the water column, making them a valuable sentinel model for assessing impacts of pelagic exposure. Sea urchin gametes were exposed to H₂O₂ (1 mM, 10 min) and evaluated for DNA damage (strand breaks, oxidised nucleotides, and total cytosine methylation) by the modified fast micromethod and cross-fertilized to produce sea urchin embryos to assess DNA damage and developmental anomalies. A significant increase of DNA damage with strand scission factor of up to 0.11 ± 0.01 (mean ± SD) was detected in blastula embryos (age 24 h) and up to 0.10 ± 0.01 (mean ± SD) in re-exposed blastula embryos fertilised from unexposed eggs and exposed (1 mM H2O2) sperm. No significant differences in total methylation were detected in any cross-fertilisation treatments after gamete exposure, but there was a non-significant trend in hypermethylation in embryos fertilised from unexposed eggs and exposed sperm, suggesting that paternal exposure to H₂O₂ poses a grater genotoxic risk to developing embryos than maternal exposure. The consequences of hypermethylation for larval development and survival remain unresolved. Integrating measures of DNA damage with epigenetic methylation changes across the gamete-embryo transition and early embryonic development provides critical insight into cross-generational mechanistic impacts of genotoxicants on ecologically critical broadcast spawning species in marine ecosystems.
journal: Mutation research. Genetic toxicology and environmental mutagenesis

title: Intrapartum Maternal Glycemic Trajectories and the Risk of Neonatal Hypoglycemia in Type 1 Diabetes Pregnancies: A Granular Continuous Glucose Monitoring Analysis.
abstract: To investigate the longitudinal relationship between intrapartum maternal glycemic trajectories and the development of neonatal hypoglycemia (NH) in pregnancies complicated by type 1 diabetes (T1D). This prospective observational study enrolled 31 pregnant women with pre-gestational T1D managed via multiple daily injections or manual insulin pump therapy. High-resolution maternal glucose trends were tracked using continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) and aligned retrospectively backward from umbilical cord clamping. Maternal glucose over time was analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model. Predictive performance and optimal clinical thresholds were evaluated via Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis. NH occurred in 15 out of 31 newborns (48.4%). Longitudinal mixed-effects modeling revealed a significant group x time interaction (P <0.01), with maternal glycemic trajectories in the NH group significantly diverging from the euglycemic cohort starting at the 6-hour pre-delivery window (119 +/- 13 vs. 104 +/- 11 mg/dL, corrected P = 0.002). ROC analysis demonstrated that predictive power peaked during the terminal 2 hours of labor (Area Under the Curve, AUC = 0.88). In multivariable logistic regression adjusted for large-for-gestational-age (LGA) status, terminal maternal glucose emerged as the sole independent predictor of NH (Odds Ratio = 6.72 per 10 mg/dL increase, 95% CI: 1.05-1.40; P <0.01). Intrapartum maternal glucose trajectories significantly associate with immediate neonatal metabolic transition. Stricter peripartum glycemic control starting at least 6 hours before expected delivery may help mitigate the risk of a terminal fetal insulin surge and subsequent hypoglycemia, targeting standard consensus-based ranges.
journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists

title: Oxytocin receptor activation enhances SK channel-mediated afterhyperpolarization in MPOA neurons of maternally experienced mice.
abstract: Maternal experience induces significant behavioral changes; however, the underlying cellular mechanisms within the medial preoptic area (MPOA), a central hub for regulating maternal behavior, remain poorly understood. Here, we combined behavioral assays (e.g., pup retrieval, crouching, nesting, and grooming) with in vitro whole-cell patch-clamp recordings to examine how maternal experience alters the intrinsic excitability of MPOA neurons and to identify the underlying mechanisms. Adult female mice were divided into three groups: virgin females, dams (experienced dams), and co-housed virgins (virgins co-housed with a dam and her pups for five days). Maternal behavior and the intrinsic properties of MPOA neurons were assessed in all three groups. We first compared virgin females with experienced dams, and then tested whether the maternal experience-dependent changes in MPOA neurons were reproduced in co-housed virgins by social co-housing. Our results revealed that MPOA neurons from both dams and co-housed virgins exhibited reduced excitability and increased afterhyperpolarization (AHP) amplitude. This enhancement was mediated by small-conductance calcium-activated potassium (SK) channels, as it was abolished by the SK channel blocker apamin. Furthermore, direct application of an oxytocin receptor agonist to MPOA neurons from virgin females induced similar functional changes, replicating the physiological profile observed in dams. Notably, this oxytocin-induced enhancement of SK channel activity was observed in glutamatergic, but not GABAergic, MPOA neurons, indicating that the effect is not uniform across cell types. These findings suggest that oxytocin modulates SK channel activity to reduce the excitability of a subpopulation of MPOA neurons. Because this effect was prominent in VGLUT2-positive neurons, it may facilitate maternal behavior by reducing the activity of neurons that restrain maternal behavior, a candidate mechanism by which hormonal and experiential signals converge on MPOA excitability.

title: The effect of maternal oxygenation on cardiopulmonary haemodynamics during the transition at birth in preterm lambs.
abstract: The cardiovascular transition at birth is a period of instability for preterm infants; however, the impact of fetal oxygen (PaO2) levels on this process is unclear. We hypothesized that increasing maternal, and subsequently, fetal oxygenation will increase pulmonary blood flow (PBF) and improve cardiovascular stability at birth. Preterm sheep fetuses (0.9 gestation) were delivered via cesarean section and instrumented to measure carotid pressure and flow, PBF, and cerebral (SctO2) and arterial (SaO2) oxygenation. Ewes were randomized to maternal oxygen supplementation (O2Supp; fetal PaO2 > 20 mmHg, n = 7) or reduction (O2Red; PaO2 < 20 mmHg, n = 8). After reaching target PaO2, lambs underwent immediate cord clamping, with ventilation withheld for 1 min, then maintained for 30 min. O2Supp increased fetal pH, PaO2, SpO2, SctO2, and PBF (28.5 ± 7.8 vs 4.0 ± 3.2 mL/min/kg), which was maintained during the period between cord clamping and ventilation. Cord clamping increased blood pressure but reduced oxygenation in O2Supp lambs. Ventilation caused marked increases in carotid pressure and flow in O2Red lambs, which were attenuated by prior oxygen supplementation. Maternal oxygen supplementation enhances fetal oxygenation and PBF before cord clamping and reduces cardiovascular instability, suggesting potential benefits for improving cardiovascular stability in preterm infants. The impact of maternal and fetal oxygenation on the cardiovascular transition is not known. We found that maternal oxygen supplementation improves fetal oxygen and increases pulmonary blood flow prior to cord clamping. Maternal oxygen supplementation stabilizes carotid blood pressure and flow during cord clamping and ventilation onset. Our findings suggest that maternal oxygen supplementation may provide cardiovascular stability for preterm infants at birth.

title: Treatment sequencing for intracardiac masses in pregnancy: a 10-year retrospective cohort of 21 patients
abstract: Abstract Background Intracardiac masses during pregnancy are rare, and treatment decisions must balance timely maternal surgery against fetal exposure to cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). We evaluated a 10-year single-center experience, focusing on gestational-age-based treatment sequencing and maternal and pregnancy outcomes. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 21 women who underwent surgery for an intracardiac mass associated with pregnancy between April 2016 and July 2026. Strategies were classified by actual sequence: antenatal surgery with intended pregnancy continuation, delivery followed by cardiac surgery during the same anesthetic session, postpartum cardiac surgery, and concurrent early-pregnancy termination and surgery. Follow-up ended on 31 August 2026. Analyses were descriptive. Results Histopathology showed 19 myxomas, 1 hemangioma, and 1 lipoma. Antenatal surgery with intended pregnancy continuation was performed in 14 women at 15.8 ± 3.4 gestational weeks; delivery-prioritized management in 4 at 35–39 weeks; postpartum surgery in 2 at 49 and 57 days after delivery; and concurrent termination and surgery in 1 at 9 weeks. Mean CPB time was 55.9 ± 17.9 min; mean aortic cross-clamp time was 34.2 ± 16.1 min among 20 patients who underwent cross-clamping. There were 17 live births (81.0%), 3 terminations (14.3%), and 1 ongoing pregnancy (4.8%). No in-hospital maternal death or predefined major maternal perioperative complication occurred. Median maternal follow-up was 23.9 months (range, 1.3–124.1), with no death or tumor recurrence documented. Conclusions Individualized sequencing of cardiac surgery and delivery was associated with favorable observed outcomes in this selected surgical cohort. Antenatal resection may be considered before fetal maturity when maternal risk precludes waiting, whereas delivery before cardiac surgery may be appropriate near fetal maturity. These findings support multidisciplinary planning in experienced centers, while conclusions remain constrained by the observational design and small sample size.

title: A Young Man With Hypereosinophilia and Pseudochylothorax.
abstract: Case presentationA 31-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of dry cough, progressive dyspnea, intermittent fever, and unintentional weight loss of 8 kg. He had no wheezing, hemoptysis, chest pain, palpitations, or skin rashes. He did not smoke and reported occasional alcohol intake. One year earlier, he had been diagnosed elsewhere with pleuro-pericardial TB based on an ultrasound showing right-sided pleural effusion, and 2-dimensional echocardiography showed pericardial effusion. Pleural fluid analysis showed a lymphocytic exudative pleural effusion with elevated adenosine deaminase levels (46 IU/mL). The patient received anti-tubercular therapy along with tapering corticosteroids, showing initial clinical improvement. He was employed as a soldier in the army, and his last posting was in northeast India, where he frequently consumed raw crabs pickled in alcohol. There was no other significant environmental history.

title: Maternal separation remodels Purkinje cell circuits and impairs cerebellar synaptic plasticity
abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Early-life adversity has been associated with cerebellar abnormalities, but the cellular and circuit-level changes involved and their persistence across development remain poorly understood. We examined whether maternal separation (MS) disrupts cerebellar circuit maturation and whether these changes are accompanied by alterations in synaptic function and behavior. Methods CD1 mice underwent daily maternal separation from postnatal day 2 to 18, whereas control litters remained undisturbed. Cerebellar alterations were assessed using transcriptomic and DNA methylation profiling, RT-qPCR, immunoblotting, Purkinje-cell morphometric analysis, and VGLUT1/VGLUT2 immunofluorescence. Patch-clamp electrophysiology was used to examine synaptic transmission and plasticity. Motor coordination, spontaneous locomotion, social approach, and stress-coping behavior were also evaluated. Results RNA sequencing of whole cerebellar tissue revealed early transcriptional remodeling, involving synaptic transmission, neuronal architecture, and plasticity-related pathways. Consistent with this profile, we found that MS altered Purkinje cell dendritic arborization and excitatory input remodeling, together with deficits in cerebellar long-term synaptic plasticity and reduced BDNF-related signaling. In parallel, methylation analysis revealed hypermethylation of the glucocorticoid receptor promoter and reduced cerebellar receptor expression, indicating that early-life stress also engages stress-related epigenetic mechanisms in this region. Importantly, these neurobiological changes were associated with motor coordination deficits, altered stress-coping behavior, and impaired social interaction. Discussion These findings identify the developing cerebellum as a target of early-life adversity and suggest that disrupted cerebellar maturation may contribute to lasting functional consequences. This study extends our understanding of the effects of maternal separation beyond the brain regions traditionally associated with stress responses.

title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel Nav1.2 inhibitors as antiepileptic agents.
abstract: Voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.2 is a validated target for anticonvulsant therapy, yet Nav1.2 inhibitors remain scarce. To explore the unexplored N-4 position of the [1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine scaffold, we designed and synthesized two series of novel derivatives bearing diverse substituents at this position. Their Nav1.2 inhibitory activities were evaluated using FLIPR membrane potential and whole-cell patch-clamp assays, while their anticonvulsant efficacy and neurotoxicity were assessed in MES/ sc-PTZ seizure models and rotarod test, respectively. Structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis revealed that hydrophobic volume complementarity, rather than aromaticity, is the primary driver of Nav1.2 potency. Compound 3b, bearing a simple n-butyl group at N-4, emerged as the most promising lead, exhibiting moderate Nav1.2 inhibition (88.9% at 30 μM; FLIPR IC50 = 11.55 μM; patch-clamp IC50 = 7.62 μM for the inactivated state) and exceptional in vivo efficacy (ED50 = 9.17 mg/kg, TD50 > 813.40 mg/kg, PI >88.70) in the sc-PTZ model. Compound 3y also demonstrated moderate Nav1.2 inhibition (69.8%, IC50 = 12.19 μM) and potent anticonvulsant activity (ED50 = 13.7 mg/kg, PI >23.1). Patch-clamp electrophysiology confirmed that 3b and 3y inhibit the inactivated state of Nav1.2 (IC50 = 7.62 μM and 8.31 μM, respectively) with negligible effect on the resting state. Molecular docking and MD simulations revealed that 3b binds within the Nav1.2 pore via hydrogen bonds, π-π stacking, and hydrophobic contacts. Tissue distribution studies demonstrated efficient blood-brain barrier penetration (brain-to-plasma ratio of 1.65 at 1 h post-dose). Although 3b showed limited stability in human and rat liver microsomes (T1/2 = 12.20 and 10.65 min, respectively), its potent in vivo efficacy and exceptionally high protective index support its continued optimization and preclinical development as a promising candidate for epilepsy therapy.

title: Exceptional preservation reveals the deep-time reproductive ecology and trophic breadth of Early Cretaceous viviparid gastropods.
abstract: Direct empirical evidence regarding the reproductive biology and trophic strategies of ancient freshwater invertebrates remains scarce due to the typical loss of internal anatomical and dietary records. Here, we report an exceptionally preserved assemblage of the freshwater snail 'Viviparus' sp. from the Lower Cretaceous (c. 120 Ma) Kitadani Formation, central Japan. High-resolution X-ray micro-computed tomography and microfossil extraction reveal key ecological adaptations: obligate ovoviviparity with up to 16 embryonic shells showing an axial developmental size gradient within the maternal body whorl, female-biased sexual size dimorphism, and continuous indeterminate growth. Analyses of gastrointestinal residues and taphonomic associations further indicate trophic flexibility (epilithic microalgal grazing, suspension feeding, and detritivory) alongside opportunistic microhabitat use within articulated unionid bivalves. This high-fidelity preservation-retaining delicate embryonic shells, intact protoconchs, and organic residues-is linked to a distinctive taphonomic window, wherein alkaline ash from palaeo-wildfires is inferred to have buffered ambient freshwater acidity, mitigating post-mortem carbonate dissolution. Our findings demonstrate that modern-type viviparid reproductive and feeding adaptations were already established by the Early Cretaceous, illustrating how wildfire-mediated geochemical buffering can preserve rare biological records in Mesozoic limnic ecosystems.

title: A Nontoxin Aminopyrimidine Probe for Near State-Independent NaV1.7 Inhibition.
abstract: The voltage-gated sodium channel NaV1.7 is among the most compelling genetically validated pain targets; however, advanced small-molecule inhibitors, including voltage-sensing domain IV (VSD4)-directed series, have not yet achieved robust clinical efficacy, potentially reflecting pharmacological limitations such as pronounced state dependence. Here, we report a nontoxin aminopyrimidine series that serves as a differentiated pharmacological probe for near state-independent NaV1.7 inhibition. Using a high-throughput automated patch clamp screening cascade designed to deprioritize established local anesthetic pore binders, we identified hit 1 and optimized it to compound 6, which combines balanced resting- and inactivated-state potency (IC50 = 1.00 and 0.45 μM, respectively). It displays a 29-fold selectivity margin over NaV1.5 and a tetrodotoxin (TTX)-like isoform profile that includes comparable activity on NaV1.7 and NaV1.1. Structure-activity studies identified the aminopyrimidine core and methylene-linked aniline motif as key determinants of this profile, while NaV mutant profiling supports a functional fingerprint consistent with pore-proximal modulation distinct from VSD4-directed inhibition.

title: Fertilisation Success in Acanthaster cf. solaris and Acanthaster brevispinus and Reciprocal Hybrid Crosses Across a Range of Sperm Concentrations and Development to the Hybrid Juvenile.
abstract: Novel species interactions between resident and range shifting species in response to warming are posing challenges for conservation and management. This is especially the case when major predatory species are involved, as seen in the appearance of a mixed species outbreak of coral-eating crown-of-thorns sea stars Acanthaster cf. solaris (As) and the lesser-known Acanthaster brevispinus (Ab) in the tropical to subtropical transition zone in eastern Australia. The outbreak consisted of reproductively mature animals, and we investigated the potential for cross-species hybridisation in fertilisation experiments across a range of sperm concentrations to sperm limitation conditions (106-102 sperm mL-1). Fertilisation was successful in all combinations of parents (As ♂ × As ♀, Ab ♂ × Ab ♀, Ab ♀ × As ♂, As ♀ × Ab ♂) with successful hybrid crosses in sperm dilutions as low as 102 sperm ml-1. Development in conspecific and heterospecific crosses was similar through the bipinnaria and brachiolaria larval stages to the juvenile. Juvenile hybrids had typical juvenile Acanthaster spp. development with a stellate five-armed profile post metamorphosis, gaining arms after ~78 days. At no stage did the juvenile hybrids develop the distinctive pink colour trait that is characteristic of Acanthaster cf. solaris juveniles. Our results indicate that hybridisation is not restricted by sperm limitation conditions, with subsequent development of hybrids to the advanced juvenile stage. Our results highlight the potential for hybridisation and species introgression when range shifting species overlap with sister taxa. This may facilitate further range expansion or development of resilient hybrid progeny as a risk to vulnerable high latitude coral communities.

title: Reproductive-state and life-stage variation in oxyregulation of reef-building corals.
abstract: Accelerating ocean deoxygenation driven by ocean warming, eutrophication, and water column stratification poses a global threat to coral reef ecosystems. Several large-scale coral mortality events have been documented on reefs in response to periods of severe hypoxia, wherein environmental dissolved oxygen (DO) levels are insufficient for maintaining physiological homeostasis and supporting coral health. Although adult corals have the capacity for oxyregulation, the extent to which such capacity is affected by reproduction or during coral larval life stages remains poorly understood. Here, we examined oxygen consumption patterns of eight coral species and the offspring of four of these species using closed system respirometry to characterise oxyregulatory performance before and after spawning. Adult corals exhibited a significant increase in oxyregulatory capacity, exerting their maximum regulation capacity (P cmax ) at a lower DO partial pressure ( p O 2 ) one week following spawning relative to the 1–2 days preceding gamete release, indicating heightened vulnerability of gravid colonies to hypoxia. Coral larvae also exhibited capacity for oxyregulation, albeit at a lowered capacity (i.e., less regulation possible above oxyconformity based on total positive regulation, T pos ) compared to adults, and larval performance did not correlate with conspecific adult responses. These results highlight ontogenetic and reproductive-state oxyregulation variability, suggesting critical variation in metabolic responses to DO availability across life stages. Characterising coral life stage-specific responses to altered DO availability provides important physiological context for understanding how coral reef organisms may respond to ongoing and future ocean deoxygenation.

title: Exercise and insulin independently stimulate galactose uptake into human skeletal muscle.
abstract: Carbohydrate choice affects glycaemic responses during and after exercise, particularly for individuals with impaired glucose regulation. Galactose causes smaller glycaemic excursions than glucose but is thought to require hepatic conversion to glucose via the Leloir pathway before peripheral use. Whether galactose is directly taken up by skeletal muscle, and whether this is regulated by exercise and insulin remains unclear. In this randomised, controlled crossover trial, eight healthy men (age 68 ± 4 years; body mass index 24.7 ± 2.1 kg/m2) completed two 4 h study days, with and without a hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic clamp (1.0 mU/kg/min). Galactose turnover was assessed using a primed-constant galactose infusion. Participants performed one-legged, high-intensity knee-extension exercise at maximal capacity, with the contralateral leg as a non-exercised control. Skeletal muscle galactose uptake was quantified by dynamic [1 8F]FDGal positron emission tomography (PET), and arteriovenous (AV) exchange across the leg was determined from femoral blood samples combined with [1 5O]H2O PET-measured leg perfusion. Exercise and insulin markedly increased galactose uptake (exercise effect: P < 0.001; insulin effect: P < 0.001; interaction: P = 0.0769). PET analysis showed that exercise primarily increased tracer influx (K1), while insulin increased intracellular trapping (k3) and modestly reduced efflux (k2). Plasma galactose concentrations were low (0.2 ± 0.1 mmol/L) and galactose AV exchange across the leg did not differ across conditions. Human skeletal muscle can directly take up galactose, and this is stimulated by exercise and insulin. This challenges the assumption that hepatic conversion is required before peripheral utilisation. Future studies should determine whether galactose is incorporated into skeletal muscle glycogen to a physiologically relevant extent. KEY POINTS: Galactose causes smaller spikes in blood sugar than glucose, and it has long been assumed that the body must first convert galactose into glucose in the liver before peripheral use. Using positron emission tomography imaging with the galactose analogue 2-[1 8F]fluoro-2-deoxygalactose in combination with a one-legged knee-extension ergometer, we demonstrated that human skeletal muscle can directly take up galactose. Both exercise and insulin markedly increased skeletal muscle galactose uptake, with an additive effect when combined. Exercise primarily increased galactose uptake by enhancing muscle blood flow, whereas insulin exerted its effect by promoting phosphorylation and intracellular trapping. Further studies are required to determine whether galactose is incorporated into skeletal muscle glycogen to a physiologically meaningful extent.

title: Three More Poecilogonous Sacoglossans: Why Is Egg-Size Dimorphism Generally Rare Except in One Lineage of Sea Slugs?
abstract: Theory and meta-analyses suggest changes from feeding to non-feeding larvae in marine animals may be an adaptation to conditions such as ocean productivity or circulation, but testing such predictions is difficult because intraspecific dimorphism in larval type (poecilogony) is rare. In gastropods, known examples are three caenogastropods and six heterobranch sea slugs, including five of ∼400 species in clade Sacoglossa. Here, we describe poecilogony in three more photosynthetic sea slugs from the Western Atlantic: Elysia velutinus, Elysia subornata, and Elysia papillosa. Data on egg and larval shell sizes were collected for both developmental morphs, and molecular analyses confirmed individuals differing in larval type were conspecific. Planktotrophic larvae of E. velutinus were cultured to metamorphosis and compared with lecithotrophic larvae in settlement assays. Poecilogonous taxa expressed planktotrophy in areas of enhanced productivity, but were lecithotrophic in enclosed lagoons or strong, asymmetric current regimes where circulation could limit successful dispersal. A meta-analysis of egg size and development mode data for 437 heterobranch and 57 calyptraeid species revealed that sacoglossans have unusually small lecithotrophic eggs. We hypothesize that the compressed range of egg sizes explains why poecilogony is 200 times more frequent in Sacoglossa than other gastropod clades. Traits such as suctorial feeding, kleptoplasty, and maternal investment in yolk reserves may offset fitness costs of smaller eggs in Sacoglossa. Our findings highlight new systems for studying transitions in life-history evolution, including intermediate larval forms and links between the environment and expression of development mode.

title: Effect of Prophylactic Tranexamic Acid on Perioperative Blood Loss in High-Risk Cesarean Delivery: A Randomized Controlled Study
abstract: Abstract Background Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) remains a major cause of maternal morbidity and mortality. Although tranexamic acid (TXA) is recommended for the treatment of established PPH, the clinical benefit of its prophylactic administration during cesarean delivery, particularly in women at increased risk of hemorrhage, remains uncertain. Methods Women aged 18–45 years with American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status II and at increased risk of PPH who were scheduled for elective cesarean delivery under spinal or general anesthesia were enrolled. The anesthesia technique was selected before randomization. Participants were subsequently stratified by anesthesia type and randomized within each stratum to receive either 1 g intravenous TXA after umbilical cord clamping or no TXA. All patients received a standardized uterotonic regimen. The primary outcome was estimated blood loss calculated using perioperative hematocrit values. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of blood loss > 500 and > 1000 mL, blood transfusion, perioperative changes in hemoglobin and hematocrit, additional uterotonic requirements, adverse events, and thromboembolic events during the three-month follow-up period. Eighty-four women were enrolled, and 83 were included in the final analysis. Results Estimated blood loss was 511 mL in the spinal anesthesia–TXA group, 590 mL in the spinal anesthesia control group, 579 mL in the general anesthesia–TXA group, and 617 mL in the general anesthesia control group. No statistically significant differences were observed among the groups in estimated blood loss, the incidence of blood loss > 500 or > 1000 mL, transfusion requirements, perioperative hemoglobin or hematocrit changes, or additional uterotonic use (all P > 0.05). Adverse-event rates were also comparable among groups. No thromboembolic events were identified during the three-month follow-up period. Conclusions In women at increased risk of PPH undergoing elective cesarean delivery, 1 g intravenous TXA administered after umbilical cord clamping was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in estimated blood loss or other hemorrhage-related outcomes under either spinal or general anesthesia. Given the limited sample size, the absence of statistically significant differences should be interpreted cautiously and does not exclude a potential prophylactic benefit of TXA. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07870499. Registered on October 6, 2026. Retrospectively registered.

title: SPR-based analysis of the interaction of actinoporin from the sea anemone Heteractis crispa with lipid bilayers.
abstract: Sea anemone actinoporins are the proteins belonging to the family of α-pore-forming toxins. They attract considerable interest as potential components for immunotoxins used in cancer therapy, adjuvants in the development of vaccines to enhance the immune response, and for the creation of biosensor systems based on protein nanopores. The only identified cellular target for actinoporins is the cytoplasmic membrane of eukaryotic cells, containing sphingomyelin (SM). In this study, using surface plasmon resonance (SPR) technology, we have investigated the interaction between the actinoporin RTX-A from the sea anemone Heteractis crispa and lipid bilayer membranes (BLMs), both with and without SM. We have found that RTX-A interacts with BLMs regardless of the presence of SM. In the case of SM-containing BLMs, the sensorgrams reflect the sum of two independent interactions: the analyte (RTX-A) binding to two distinct ligands, phosphatidylcholine (PC) and SM, with Kd values of approximately 10-8 M and 4.6×10-9 M, respectively. The presence of SM in the BLMs did not affect the affinity of the interaction between RTX-A and PC.

title: Resolution of COVID-19 Chemosensory Loss Upon COVID-19 Reinfection.
abstract: IntroductionThe pandemic of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has been associated with widespread myriad chemosensory dysfunction with smell loss as high as 99% and taste loss in 89% of those studied (Kim 2021, Paderno 2020, Renaud 2020). Other chemosensory problems, occur often in combination, including dysgeusia and hyposmia (3.2%), dysgeusia and anosmia (3.4%), ageusia and hyposmia (3.4%) and, ageusia and anosmia (8.5%) (Giacomelli, 2020). Hyperosmia has also been reported to be precipitated by COVID-19 infection (Di Stadio 2022, Kamali 2021). COVID-19 induced persistent hyposmia with resolution of smell and taste dysfunction with COVID-19 reinfection has not heretofore been described. Such a case is presented.MethodsTwo years prior to the presentation, a 26-year-old right-handed single male developed COVID-19 at which time his sense of smell and taste were totally eliminated. His smell gradually returned to 40-50% of normal whereby he was able to smell everything, but less intensively than he normally did. Furthermore, some odors he experienced in a hyperosmic fashion, such as smoke which was 200% more intense than normal. Prior to COVID-19 exposure, he experienced frequent flavorful eructations which were eliminated after COVID-19 exposure. His taste was initially absent after the COVID-19 exposure, but gradually returned to 60-70% of normal whereby he would taste everything but less intensively. Two years and one month after the initial COVID-19 infection despite being fully vaccinated, he contracted a recurrent COVID-19 infection. Prior to the infection, his smell and taste were 60% of normal. Acutely with the reinfection, his smell and taste ability abruptly dropped to 0% for 16 hours, after which his smell returned to 90% of normal and his taste returned to 100% of normal. During this time period, his other chemosensory problems including dysosmia, dysgeusia, cacogeusia, hyperosmia, and phantosmia all resolved, and his flavorful eructations returned. His sense of smell has remained normal for five months, but his sense of taste has gradually dropped down to 50% of normal.ResultsAbnormalities in Physical Examination: General: Scalloped tongue. Neurological Examination: Cranial Nerve (CN) Examination: CN II: Visual acuity 20/25 OU. CN III, IV, VI: left ptosis. CN V: decreased light touch left V₁ and V₂ . CN IX and X: Uvula deviates to the right. Reflexes: Absent bilateral triceps. Neuropsychiatric Testing: Clock Drawing Test: 10/10 (normal). Animal Fluency Test: 26 (normal). Go-No-Go Test: 6/6 (normal). Center for Neurologic Study Lability Scale: 8/10 (normal). Chemosensory Testing: Olfaction: After the first infection prior to the second infection: Alcohol Sniff Test: 3 (Anosmia). Chemosensory Testing: 1 month after the recurrent COVID-19: Alcohol Sniff Test: 9 (hyposmia). Brief Smell Identification Test: 9 (normosmia). Retronasal Olfaction Test: Retronasal Index: 8 (normosmia). Gustation: Phenylthiocarbamide Taste Test: 9 (normogeusia). Waterless Empirical Taste Test: sweet: 6 (normogeusia) sour: 8 (normogeusia) salty: 6 (normogeusia) bitter: 4 (hypogeusia) brothy: 0 (ageusia) total: 37 (normogeusia).ConclusionsCOVID-19 induced smell loss has been observed to worsen after reinfection, improvement has not been described (Jain, Ear, Nose & Throat Journal, 2021, Lechien, Journal of Internal Medicine, 2021). Possibly the recurrent infection induced hyperosmia which superimposed upon the underlying COVID-19 induced anosmia caused an additive effect, combining together to induce normosmia as opposed to COVID-19 induced hyposmia. This may be due to persistent inflammation of the olfactory bulbs and frontal lobes, inducing excessive neuronal sprouting and associated hyperosmia (Di Stadio, European Review for Medical and Pharmacological Sciences, 2022). Alternatively, COVID-19 may have acted on not only the olfactory nerves but rather on a central basis, enhancing neuronal firings in the anterior insula and hippocampus, areas involved with the olfactory integration and which have enhanced gray matter volume in states of hyperosmia (Wabnegger, 2019). Even though COVID-19 vaccination has been noted to worsen the chemosensory function (Konstantinidis, International Forum of Allergy & Rhinology, 2021), COVID-19 immunization induced improvement in smell has also been reported (Plaza, Annals of Neurology, 2021). It is possible that such an improvement is through infection induced activation of inflammatory immune responses which then acts on the infected olfactory bulbs to reduce pathology. The current case of COVID-19 infection enhancing smell and taste strengthens such an autoimmune explanation. In those with recurrent COVID-19 infection, query and investigation as to presence of improvement of chemosensory dysfunction is warranted.FundingNo Funding.

title: Transcriptomic analysis of flowers in an apple petalless mutant and its parents.
abstract: Apple petals are required for insect pollination, and the number of petals is an important commercial trait for ornamental apples. Owing to the relatively small number of apple mutants, the molecular mechanism underlying flower organ development in apple remains unclear. A petalless apple mutant was discovered from hybrid seedlings of 'Wanbai' crabapple × 'Huayue'. Transcriptome analysis of the petalless mutant and its two parents was conducted. A total of 5,118 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified between flowers from 'Wanbai' crabapple and the petalless mutant (WBvsH), whereas 6,886 DEGs were identified between flowers from 'Huayue' and the petalless mutant (HYvsH). A total of 1,718 and 1,640 DEGs were co-upregulated and co-downregulated respectively, in the WBvsH and HYvsH comparison groups. KEGG analysis revealed that these co-upregulated DEGs were significantly enriched in plant hormone signal transduction, circadian rhythm-plant, and photosynthesis pathways, and these co-downregulated DEGs were significantly enriched in the biosynthesis of amino acids, carbon metabolism, and glycolysis/gluconeogenesis pathways. Among these coregulated DEGs, compared with those in WB and HY, the expression of four organ identity class A genes, MdTOEL1, MdTOEL2, MdFUL2, and MdFUL1, and one organ identity class C gene, MdSTKL, were upregulated in H; the expression of three organ identity class B genes, MdAP3L1, MdAP3L2, and MdAP3L3, were downregulated in H; and the expression of the organ identity class E gene MdSEPL3 was upregulated, but the expression of MdSEPL1 and MdSEPL2 were downregulated. Yeast two-hybrid and split-luciferase complementation assays revealed that the class E protein MdSEPL1 promoted interactions between any two class B proteins; however, no interactions were detected between B proteins. This study provides comprehensive analysis of the gene expression in flowers of the two parents and the petalless mutant offspring to understand the mechanism of the formation of the petalless phenotype. In apple mutant, genes involved in auxin signaling pathway were activated and genes involved in primary metabolism pathways were inhibited. 3 floral organ identity-related AP3 orthologues were downregulated in apple mutant, suggesting that these genes may be candidate genes responsible for petal phenotype.

title: Evolutionary tuning of complexin-synaptotagmin fusion clamp governs regulated neurotransmitter release.
abstract: Synaptic vesicles must be held in a fusion-ready but restrained state until Ca²⁺ influx triggers release. Synaptotagmin-1 (Syt1) and Complexin (CPX) both contribute to this fusion clamp, yet removing either protein produces opposite effects in different species. Whether this reflects genuine divergence in their molecular roles, or species-specific tuning of a conserved mechanism, has remained unresolved. Here we address this by comparing mammalian and C. elegans orthologs in a reconstituted single-vesicle assay that isolates clamping from upstream docking and priming. We find that clamping in both species requires the combined action of CPX and Syt1, with neither sufficient on its own. CPX clamps only with its cognate SNARE complex, a specificity conferred entirely by its accessory helix. The Syt1 orthologs differ markedly in intrinsic clamping strength, which maps to C2B mediated higher-order oligomerization and sets the functional dependence on CPX in each system. These results support a dual-regulator model of exocytosis in which Syt1 and CPX act sequentially and cooperatively through discrete molecular states to control vesicle clamping and Ca²⁺-triggered release. This framework reconciles long-standing functional discrepancies across species and reveals how evolutionary divergence modulates conserved mechanisms governing synaptic fidelity.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

title: Induced encapsulated cannibalism and its physiological and morphological consequences for veligers of the gastropod Crepipatella peruviana: developmental plasticity and the evolutionary significance of intracapsular feeding
Impact of Dietary Formulation on the Gonadal Maturation and Reproductive Potential of the Broodstock Sandfish ( Holothuria scabra ) in Sea Cage Culture
abstract: Abstract The sustainable aquaculture of sandfish (Holothuria scabra), a high–value species prized for its nutritional and medicinal properties, depends on optimized broodstock management. This study investigated the impact of three dietary formulations—a commercial feed, a mix feed consisting of specifically selected ingredients (seaweed, polychaetes, and green caviar), and a mud feed—on the reproductive performance of H. scabra over six months. Results indicated that the mix feed significantly enhanced the gonadosomatic index (GSI = 0.55 ± 0.22%) and sperm viability compared to other groups (p < 0.05). Furthermore, this treatment elevated reproductive hormone levels (17β–estradiol and testosterone) and upregulated the expression of key genes, 17β–hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase and vitellogenin, by 1.8– and 2.1–fold, respectively. Histological analysis confirmed advanced gonadal maturation in % of the mix feed group. These findings demonstrate that nutritionally enriched feeds containing seaweed, polychaetes, and green caviar effectively promote gamete quality and maturation, offering a practical strategy for enhancing hatchery–based seed production. Overall, this study provides a circular, low-footprint nutritional strategy that minimizes reliance on resource-intensive commercial feeds by leveraging localized coastal bioresources. Optimizing broodstock conditioning through targeted endocrine and molecular up-regulation serves as a practical dietary framework for aquaculture to advance sustainable marine resource management, accelerating hatchery yields for ecological restocking and sustainable aquaculture development.

title: Evaluation of a prototype system for conditioning and spawning the yellow clam Amarilladesma mactroides in captivity
abstract: The development of reliable hatchery protocols is essential for the sustainable production and conservation of the yellow clam Amarilladesma mactroides , an endangered species of high ecological and socioeconomic importance in the southwestern Atlantic. This study evaluated a prototype system for the conditioning and spawning of A. mactroides under captive conditions by integrating recent advances in broodstock conditioning, feeding management, and spawning induction techniques. A total of 170 adult clams were maintained buried in a seawater recirculation system and fed a concentrated microalgae diet composed of Chaetoceros muelleri and Isochrysis galbana . Spawning was induced through thermal shock (16 to 26 °C) combined with sperm addition. After 45 days of conditioning, broodstock survival reached 94.7%, and histological analyses revealed that 100% of the individuals examined had attained gonadal maturity. Oocyte diameter was significantly higher after 45 days of conditioning than at day 0, reaching 46.9–48.7 μm, which exceeded the minimum size considered indicative of spawning readiness in yellow clams. Spawning induction resulted in the release of approximately 129 million eggs and the production of more than 30 million larvae. The use of concentrated microalgae supported satisfactory reproductive performance and high broodstock survival. Overall, the results demonstrate that a 45-day conditioning period combined with concentrated microalgae feeding and non-invasive spawning induction using thermal shock and sperm addition can support captive reproduction of A. mactroides under the experimental conditions tested. The prototype system provides a promising basis for further optimization and evaluation of hatchery protocols for the species, including their potential application to future stock enhancement and sustainable aquaculture initiatives.

title: Temporal dynamics of coral bleaching and live coral cover at the Cayman Crown Reef, Gulf of Honduras (2016–2025)
abstract: Located in the Gulf of Honduras between Guatemala and southern Belize, Cayman Crown (Corona Caimán) is a recently documented offshore coral reef system of high geomorphological complexity lying at the terminus of the deep Cayman Trench. The reef is characterized by extensive spur-and-groove formations and steep vertical walls descending from 10–30 m to depths exceeding 300 m. Despite its offshore location, Cayman Crown has historically supported among the highest live coral cover recorded across the Mesoamerican Reef (24-50%), consistently corresponding to good (≥20%) to very good (≥40%) live coral cover, under the Reef Health Index. However, the reef has been exposed to intensifying thermal stress across three successive bleaching events. It remains unknown whether this offshore reef can retain its capacity to recover under repeated thermal stress, as multi-event, site-level records of bleaching and recovery are lacking for this reef system. Here, we assess bleaching severity, mortality, and recovery across four sites spanning three bleaching events from 2016 to 2025. The highest Bleaching Severity Index (BSI) values were recorded during the 3.5 Regional Coral Bleaching Event (RCBE), 2019–2021; with a BSI of 54–59% and peak DHW ~10 °C-weeks, followed by the Fourth Global Coral Bleaching Event (GCBE), 2023–2025; with a BSI: 25–41% and peak DHW ~19 °C-weeks, and moderate values during the Third GCBE, 2014–2017; with a BSI: 25–30% and peak DHW ~8 °C-weeks. Following the 2019 bleaching, corals recovered nearly completely, demonstrating strong short-term post-disturbance resilience. In contrast, consecutive bleaching during the Fourth GCBE resulted in approximately 29% overall coral mortality and persistent residual bleaching extending into the February 2025 post-disturbance survey (BSI: 4–10%). The 2023–24 bleaching caused pronounced live coral cover losses, particularly at Corona Caimán Valle de Aga CC01 (50.3% to 34.1%) and Corona Caimán Bajón GT008 (35.7% to 22.5%), while Corona Caimán 2 CC02 showed a slight increase (24.7% to 28.3%), indicating variability in site-level responses. These findings are consistent with projections of increasing marine heatwave frequency, under which reefs would experience repeated bleaching with shorter recovery windows. The transition from near-complete recovery following a single acute bleaching disturbance to measurable colony mortality under consecutive bleaching events suggests that repeated heat stress may erode the resilience of even offshore reefs.

title: Postpartum intrusions are associated with child and maternal mental health
abstract: Abstract Intrusive thoughts of infant-related harm are a common postpartum experience, yet their relationship with maternal and infant mental health is understudied. The current analyses utilized data from 267 participants ( M = 32.2, SD = 4.6) across Australia, the UK, and the US who took part in the COVID-19 Risks Across the Lifespan (CORAL) study. The included participants were pregnant at Time 1 (May to September 2020) and completed measures of postpartum intrusions and mental health at 1–3 follow-up timepoints (up to April 2022) after giving birth. Postpartum intrusions were cross-sectionally associated with poorer maternal (anxiety and depression) and infant (negative affectivity) mental health at Time 4 (~ 1.5 years after Time 1). These associations held when controlling for covariates including antenatal stress, antenatal depression and anxiety, and infant age. Postpartum intrusions were also prospectively associated with infant negative affectivity at Time 4, as well as maternal anxiety and depression at Time 4. These findings highlight the importance of preparing expectant parents for, and further educating antenatal healthcare professionals about, the experience of postpartum intrusions.

title: Stressors and Mitigation Strategies in Farmed Aquatic Animals Across Species, Life Stages, and Farming Phases: Insights from the fair-fish Database
abstract: Aquaculture is a rapidly expanding industry that supplies a significant portion of global fish production. However, the welfare of many farmed aquatic species remains underexplored, particularly regarding their responses to stressors and the effectiveness of mitigation strategies. This study provides a systematic overview of stressors and mitigators affecting farmed aquatic animals. It is based on data from the WelfareChecks of the farm branch of the open-access fair-fish database. This database systematically compiles standardized information based on literature reviews across aquaculture- relevant species, with 88 profiles published up to April 2025. For this, we checked all profiles regarding the stress criterion. Each entry was categorized by stressor or mitigator, species, life stage (larvae/fry, juveniles, adults, spawners), farming phase (rearing, transportation, harvesting), and study type (farm or laboratory). A total of 358 stressor instances were identified, 273 of which originated from farm studies. The most frequently reported stressors were handling, crowding, and transportation, mostly investigated in juveniles and during the rearing phase. In contrast, early life stages and spawners were underrepresented. For mitigators, 98 instances were recorded (72 from farm studies), with food supplementation, anesthesia, acclimatization, and shelters being the most studied strategies, again focused mainly on juveniles during the rearing phase. Furthermore, stressors were studied in 62 species (70.5%), with Cyprinus carpio, Penaeus vannamei, and Salmo salar most frequently addressed. Mitigators appeared in only 32 species (36.4%), with Cyprinus carpio, Oreochromis niloticus, and Octopus maya most studied. These results highlight apparent gaps—particularly regarding less-studied species, early life stages, and most farming phases. This assessment provides a valuable foundation to guide future research and improve fish welfare and sustainability of aquaculture practices.

title: Development and Validation of a Rapid Neutralization Assay for Herpes Simplex Virus Type 1 Using a Recombinant copGFP Reporter Virus
abstract: Neutralizing antibody titers are important indicators of humoral immunity against herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1). However, conventional plaque reduction neutralization tests (PRNTs) are labor-intensive and time-consuming. Here, we developed a rapid 96-,well fluorescence-based neutralization assay using a recombinant HSV-1-expressing copepod green fluorescent protein (HSV-1-copGFP), constructed through CRISPR/Cas9-mediated homologous recombination. The reporter virus exhibited replication kinetics comparable to those of parental HSV-1, while next-generation sequencing revealed high genomic sequence conservation across passages P5, P8, and P10. Optimized assay conditions included 100 PFU/well and a detection window of 14–16 h post-infection. A custom Python program enabled automated quantification and visual verification of GFP-positive foci. Neutralizing antibody titers showed strong correlations with conventional PRNT in murine (R2 = 0.9814, p <0.0001) and human sera (R2 = 0.9840, p <0.0001). Bland–Altman analysis further demonstrated agreement between the methods, with mean biases of −0.03760 and 0.04266 for murine and human sera, respectively. Among 24 human samples, 14 (58.33%) were positive. Specificity testing using six HSV-2-positive and six varicella-zoster virus (VZV)-positive murine sera revealed limited HSV-2 cross-neutralization (22.67–27.33% at 1:10 dilution) and negligible VZV-associated neutralization, with no samples reaching the 50% neutralization endpoint. Overall, this assay represents a promising approach for rapid and quantitative detection of HSV-1-neutralizing antibodies, with the potential to complement conventional PRNT.

title: Atteozilosorus ferrodraco (Holotype ATZ-FD01): Complete Biomechanical, Physiological, and Genomic Blueprint of a Physics-Compliant 15-Meter Biological Apex Predator
abstract: "Anyone who thinks Titans only exist in movies and are impossible in real life—this is an ultimate creation that stands within all laws of nature and physics. A theoretical apex predator." — Umasankar Nayak Atteozilosorus ferrodraco (Holotype ATZ-FD01) is an original speculative biology and biomechanical apex predator design conceived, engineered, and authored by Umasankar Nayak on November 16, 2026. Unlike conventional fictional giant creatures that violate fundamental laws of physics and scaling, Atteozilosorus ferrodraco is engineered from first principles to resolve the Square-Cube Law, thermodynamic heat dissipation, caloric energy bottlenecks, radiation toxicity, and extreme environmental survival using strictly verified, real-world biological mechanisms.
